decisions.reason: SOL keeps the image and sense while smoothing the sentence.
SOL keeps the instantaneous moment and the dragon’s action.
SOL preserves the image in a complete, natural sentence.
“Rising in my throat” naturally conveys the groan welling up.
“The atmosphere it conveyed” naturally preserves the video’s effect.
The sentence break clarifies that the physical reactions bear witness.
“Countless years” preserves the accumulated power over a long age.
The glossary establishes Dragon as the species term.
“Its” clearly refers to the dragon’s terrifying power.
SOL replaces the source’s ink-spreading image with paint on a canvas and adds a sky-splitting roar.
SOL specifies “the sky,” where the source says the place resembled another world.
SOL keeps the lightning-strike image in natural English.
“Static-riddled” naturally conveys the noisy, glitching footage.
“As if they might crush them” preserves the clenched-fist image.
“We” fits the narrator and the people hearing the cry together.
The fragment naturally follows “we heard it” and preserves the dragon’s cry.
SOL drops the source’s reference to Will reaching the level of will.
SOL’s ellipsis is a natural rendering of the spoken pause.
“Escaped me in a groan” keeps the words’ involuntary delivery.
“Vanished” preserves the source’s sudden disappearance of the roar.
SOL keeps the sudden silence and peaceful impression.
The split sentences retain both the descending dragonkin and the clinging monsters.
“From high above” preserves the fall from the distant sky without awkward phrasing.
“Roared with joy and bloodlust” keeps both emotions in a brisk phrase.
“All in reverence” naturally connects their kneeling and display of respect.
“On my soul and in my name” preserves the oath in natural English.
The omitted “suddenly” does not alter the realization or its timing.
“More horrific than any you have ever seen” preserves the threat’s comparison.
“I hadn’t seen everything coming” naturally conveys that he failed to predict all of it.
SOL recasts the two humans as “worth nothing,” shifting the source’s comparison of their price to billions of lives.
“Make them kneel” preserves the command in natural English.
SOL preserves both the obsidian-black eyes and their abyss-like swirl.
“Composure” changes the recovery of societal stability into emotional calm.
SOL drops the source’s ladder-of-salvation image.
The direct imperative keeps the comment’s urgent warning and voice.
“A target” is the natural generic phrasing and keeps the joke’s meaning.
“Without so much as an ordinary joke” preserves the boards’ frozen atmosphere.
“Everyone” preserves the source’s meaning without changing the emphasis.
“The savior of a new age” and “no grand description” preserve the source’s praise.
SOL preserves the sequence of filling Taemin’s place, making it his own, and saving lives.
SOL preserves that the warning reached the Pentagon and the rest of the world without adding an unstated sender.
“Futile … before the vast army” keeps the contrast between brief hope and invasion.
“Make them kneel” preserves the command in natural English.
“Cowardly” directly preserves the source’s judgment of what survival can make people.
“While” preserves the contrast between the enraged and the silent.
“Hid their opinions” naturally conveys concealing their views to avoid criticism.
“Another half day passed” preserves the elapsed time and transition.
SOL shifts “at last” from the army’s seizure and advance to the people’s silence.
“Say it aloud” loses the source’s point that they could not say it to anyone.
